text:
amy: FYI premerge CI blocked PR #512 because keystore-policy.yaml diff removed a service account binding. 

sam: saw that. The linter flagged it as high-risk. It refused to merge until SECURITY signoff.

amy: Error from CI:
```
premerge-check: keystore-policy.yaml removed binding for serviceAccount:scanner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com -> BLOCKING (requires SEC_APPROVAL)
```

oscar: I removed the binding to narrow scope per audit, but didn't realize the scanner SA was still needed by SAST/DFAST upload flow. My bad.

nina: This pattern keeps happening. Proposal: require a signed-change marker in PR body when touching keystore-policy.yaml, and a git hook that enforces it. E.g., `KESTORE-CHANGE:SEC-<ticket>`

sam: +1. Also let's add an automated premerge lint that runs `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` against a test key and fails the PR if scanner SA is not present. That avoids surprise breakage.

amy: For immediate triage, CI producers hit failures in ~3 pipelines yesterday; we need a safer fallback for triage: write unencrypted artifacts to an ephemeral bucket with strict ACL and lifecycle 24h. Security will audit those writes.

oscar: we can automate bucket creation during incident with a script. Example command:
```
gsutil mb -p redwood-prod -l US-CENTRAL1 gs://tmp-sdlc-artifacts-${BUILD_ID}
gsutil iam ch group:security@redwood.com:objectAdmin gs://tmp-sdlc-artifacts-${BUILD_ID}
gsutil lifecycle set lifecycle.json gs://tmp-sdlc-artifacts-${BUILD_ID}
```

nina: lifecycle.json should enforce Delete after 1 day. Make sure encryption-at-rest is still on at bucket-level, but we can't rely on KMS keys in this fail path. Also require that CI adds header `x-incident-id:INC-2026-820`.

sec-bot: Alert: keystore-policy-change-detected - created INC-2026-820. Follow-up ticket SEC-700 created for premerge enforcement.

sam: SEC-700 should include: premerge linter, PR body marker check, CODEOWNERS lock for keystore-policy.yaml, and a smoke test that runs `gcloud kms keys test-iam-permissions` for roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter.

amy: Also add SIEM rule: if any SetIamPolicy on `keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*` occurs, create a high-priority finding and page security oncall. Use Cloud Audit Logs filter: 
```
resource.type="kms_keyring"
protoPayload.methodName="SetIamPolicy"
```

oscar: Can we also emit a signed commit artifact when updating keystore-policy.yaml so we can roll back easily? E.g., tag commit with `keystore-rollback-<sha>` automatically.

nina: Good idea. We'll add a small GitHub Action that creates a rollback tag and attaches a brief changelog to the ticket.

sam: For evidence/forensics: proposal to enrich artifact metadata with `pr=<PR_NUM> commit=<SHA> author=<user>` and include `kms_access_log_id` if available so postmortems can correlate object ingestion with KMS decrypt calls.

amy: Compliance asked for 90 days of KMS access-log retention and 365 days for artifact provenance metadata. Let's capture that in SEC-700 scope.

oscar: One more ops safety net: add a unit/integration test in CI that spins up a mock KMS (or uses test project) and asserts the scanner service account has decrypt permission before allowing merges to master.

nina: I'll own the GH Action and SEC-700 details. sam you own the linter and smoke test. amy will draft the incident runbook snippet for ephemeral bucket fallback and rollback tag steps.

sec-bot: INC-2026-820 mitigated by attach: rollback-tag + rebind. SEC-700 opened and assigned to nina/sam/amy.
